'''Woodside''' is a neighborhood in the western portion of the [[borough (New York City)|borough]] of [[Queens]] in [[New York City]]. It is bordered on the south by [[Maspeth, Queens|Maspeth]], on the north by [[Astoria, Queens|Astoria]], on the west by [[Sunnyside, Queens|Sunnyside]], and on the east by [[Elmhurst, Queens|Elmhurst]], [[Jackson Heights, Queens|Jackson Heights]], and [[East Elmhurst, Queens|East Elmhurst]]. Some areas are widely residential and very quiet, while other parts, especially the ones around [[Roosevelt Avenue]], are busier.

In the 19th century the area was part of the Town of Newtown (now [[Elmhurst, Queens|Elmhurst]]). The adjacent area of Winfield was largely incorporated into the post office serving Woodside and as a consequence Winfield lost much of its identity distinct from Woodside. However, with large-scale residential development in the 1860s, Woodside became the largest [[Irish American]] community in Queens, being approximately 80% Irish by the 1930s and maintaining a strong Irish culture today. In the early 1990s, many [[Asian American]] families include a large [[Filipinos in the New York metropolitan area|Filipino community]] moved into the area, and as a result the current population is 30% Asian American. [[South Asian]]s and [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latino]]s have also moved to Woodside in recent years.

Reflecting the neighborhood’s long-standing cultural diversity, the area offers a wide range of international restaurants, cafés, and pubs. It is particularly known for its [[Thai food|Thai]],  [[Filipino food|Filipino]], and [[Cuisine of South America|South American]] dining options, which contribute to the neighborhood’s varied and distinctive culinary scene.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/11/03/dining/a-thai-pilgrimage-leads-to-queens.html |title=A Thai Pilgrimage Leads to Queens |last=Bruni |first=Frank |date=November 3, 2004 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331 |access-date=January 22, 2019 |language=en-US |archive-date=January 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122145034/https://www.nytimes.com/2004/11/03/dining/a-thai-pilgrimage-leads-to-queens.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/15/nyregion/thecity/15joll.html |title=Filipino "Soul Food" Comes to Queens |last=Foggin |first=Mark |date=February 13, 2009 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331 |access-date=January 22, 2019 |language=en-US |archive-date=January 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122145006/https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/15/nyregion/thecity/15joll.html |url-status=live }}</ref>Woodside is located in [[Queens Community Board 2|Queens Community District 2]] and its ZIP Code is 11377.<ref name="NYCPlanning" /> It is patrolled by the [[New York City Police Department]]'s 108th Precinct.<ref name="NYPD 108th Precinct" /> Politically, Woodside is represented by the [[New York City Council]]'s 22nd and 26th Districts.<ref>[http://www.nyc.gov/html/dc/downloads/pdf/queens.pdf Current City Council Districts for Queens County] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161222003335/http://www.nyc.gov/html/dc/downloads/pdf/queens.pdf |date=December 22, 2016 }}, [[New York City]]. Accessed May 5, 2017.</ref>
